stories.title: The hour of driving is the product
stories.html:
Batching a groomer's day by neighbourhood saves about an hour of driving; that hour is the whole pitch.

A groomer does not buy a booking form, she buys back an hour of her afternoon. Everything else in the app exists to protect it.

stories.title: Fifty customers before calendar sync
stories.html:
Do not build calendar sync before fifty customers; the first forty never asked for it.

Every early feature request feels urgent. The ones that come from your ten happiest customers are worth building; the ones that come from a hunch are worth a note.

stories.title: Port Alder groomers: what a route day looks like
stories.html:
A route day in Port Alder starts at seven with the van's tanks filled and ends at five with a wash of the van itself, and in between there are six to nine stops.

The best days are the ones where the neighbourhoods line up and the worst are the ones with a cancelled first slot.

stories.title: Grandfathering, explained to a groomer
stories.html:
Grandfathering means the price you signed up at is the price you keep, even when the price for new customers goes up.

I explain it to groomers with a van analogy: the fuel price changed at the pump, but the tank you already filled is still full.

stories.title: Why the van has a name
stories.html:
Delia's van is called Biscuit, and customers ask for the van by name, which is a small piece of marketing that no software could invent.

stories.title: The two-hour text
stories.html:
A reminder text two hours before the slot gets a reply; the one the night before gets ignored, and that is worth a whole afternoon of tuning.

stories.title: What a deposit does to a calendar
stories.html:
A small deposit turns a calendar of maybes into a calendar of promises, and that change is felt by both the groomer and the dog owner.

stories.title: The seven-day payout nobody warns you about
stories.html:
The first Stripe payout takes about seven days, and a groomer who is not told will assume the money is lost, so we now say it before signup.

stories.title: Vet clinic cards that get used
stories.html:
Vet clinics hand out a printable card with their own name on it, and it works because the clinic is vouching for the groomer, not for us.

stories.title: Why two-van shops stay
stories.html:
Two-van shops stay because the second van needs the calendar, and a shared calendar is the one thing a paper diary cannot do.

stories.title: Forty-one groomers
stories.html:
Forty-one groomers is not a big number, but every one of them has a name, a van and a phone number that I know by heart.
